exposure: Delivery characteristics (prolonged rupture of membranes, fetal distress, prematurity, birth weight, multiple gestation, low 5-min APGAR score)
outcome: Neonatal outcomes (NICU admission, respiratory complications, sepsis, mortality, length of hospitalization)
cohort: 2,595 women and their neonates delivered by cesarean section at King Abdullah University Hospital (KAUH) in Jordan between January 2016 and July 2017
finding: Cesarean section rates are high at this Jordanian institution, with almost one-third of neonates delivered via cesarean section requiring NICU admission, highlighting the need for strategies to optimize delivery practices and reduce associated morbidities.
birth_weight: Low birth weight was associated with increased risk of NICU admission
